rows.title: Colorado’s minimum-wage increases benefit economy, but many workers are still struggling
rows.standfirst: A full-time worker must put in 104 hours per week at the state’s current minimum wage to afford a two-bedroom rental in Colorado

rows.title: Six more Colorado communities consider raising their minimum wage
rows.standfirst: A 2019 state law allows local governments to set their own starting point higher than the state’s current $14.40 hourly minimum.

rows.title: Democrats at the Colorado Capitol have had enough of the ballot-measure leverage dance
rows.standfirst: Ballot measures backed by wealthy interests prompted the governor and lawmakers to cut deals time and again this year, most recently leading to the special session on property taxes last week

rows.title: Colorado is having one of its worst grasshopper infestations in recent history. Here’s what people are doing about it.
rows.standfirst: The insects are chewing through lettuce in city gardens and mowing down farmers’ crops on the plains

rows.title: How rebates, tax credits cut the cost of solar by $5,000 for one Colorado couple
rows.standfirst: Interest rates have driven rooftop solar costs sky high, but tax credits and rebates bring arrays back within reach

rows.title: More than 15,500 business filings in Colorado deemed fraudulent were made by one guy
rows.standfirst: The Attorney General’s Office said the filings linked to one Northglenn address were made when filing fees were reduced to $1, at a cost of $765,919 to taxpayers. There could be more.

rows.title: CEOs of Albertsons and Kroger says shoppers would see lower prices after merger
rows.standfirst: Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen and Albertsons CEO Vivek Sankaran appeared in Oregon’s U.S. District Court to testify against the Federal Trade Commission’s attempt to block the proposed merger of their companies

rows.title: 3 Colorado utilities are getting $1.1B from the feds to accelerate the move to renewable energy
rows.standfirst: Tri-State received the largest Inflation Reduction Act award and says $679M will help it exceed Colorado greenhouse gas reduction goals

rows.title: Is racism fueling claims about a Venezuelan gang “takeover” of apartment buildings in Aurora?
rows.standfirst: Anti-immigrant backlash is nothing new, say sociology and criminology experts, who point to attacks against Irish, Italian and Polish immigrants about 100 years ago

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado homeowners insurance increased nearly 60% in five years
rows.standfirst: Hail damage, wildfires and weather are only partly to blame, says industry trade group. There’s also “social inflation.” Plus: Readers and inflation, hospitality careers, and more!

rows.title: Wrecked rain gauges. Whistleblowers. Million-dollar payouts and manhunts. Then a Colorado crop fraud got really crazy.
rows.standfirst: The sordid story of two ranchers who conspired to falsify drought numbers by tampering with rain gauges on the plains of Colorado and Kansas, resulting in millions in false insurance claims

rows.title: Colorado child care declines in quality, reliability as advocates sound alarm over private equity groups moving in
rows.standfirst: Child care is more costly in Colorado than most places in the country and slots are short, which makes it a target for investors. Some say guardrails are needed as government funding increases.

rows.title: Commerce City neighbors fighting plans to store more gasoline across the street from a school
rows.standfirst: Adams 14 lawyer calls plans to add five huge tanks to a battery of 20 used to store cleaner-burning summer blend fuel near Dupont Elementary an extension of “a century of environmental racism”

rows.title: Xcel drained its $94M energy efficiency budget after marijuana growers took notice — and wants $34M more
rows.standfirst: “Unexpectedly high customer interest” led Xcel to pull the plug on a program helping businesses green their operations — for now.

rows.title: Does Denver have too many gas stations? City Council pushes new limits to save space for affordable housing.
rows.standfirst: A proposed ordinance would build buffers between new gas stations, mass transit stops and housing

rows.title: Boulder selected as 1 of 3 finalists to host Sundance Film Festival in 2027
rows.standfirst: Cincinnati and a joint bid from Park City and Salt Lake City are also on the finalist list to host the 10-day festival

rows.title: Gasoline company suddenly withdraws expansion plan for tanks across from Commerce City elementary school
rows.standfirst: Proposal drew fierce opposition to new air pollution; ONEOK blames customer decision, “tanks are no longer necessary”

rows.title: AI is growing fast. Here’s how Colorado is trying to keep up.
rows.standfirst: The state and city of Denver take cautious approach to generative AI, as local innovators develop impressive tech

rows.title: What’s Working: Techstars Denver spotlights tech startups tackling workforce issues
rows.standfirst: The disconnect between finding good workers and good jobs may just need an infusion of tech. Denver program helps speed things up. Plus: Readers share their work woes.

rows.title: Denver’s newly homeless can soon receive guidance and resources from others who used to live on the streets
rows.standfirst: The neighborhood resource hub, which is expected to launch in early 2025, will link those in need to critical services, such as housing, healthcare, job services and help with credit card debt

rows.title: Colorado’s multimillion dollar investment in quantum gets 70-acre campus in Arvada
rows.standfirst: Millions committed to new Quantum COmmons campus includes build out of shared clean-room facilities, labs and offices as part of Colorado’s quantum computing Tech Hub

rows.title: WM’s $100 million Denver East sorting center aims to boost Colorado recycling
rows.standfirst: Gov. Jared Polis and local officials break ground on massive complex to support surge in state’s “circular economy” effort

rows.title: Xcel gas bills drop almost 12% for the rest of 2024 as wholesale prices remain low
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s largest utility will pass on savings as it seeks a permanent rate increase starting in February

rows.title: Artificial intelligence takes center stage at Denver’s inaugural DenAI Summit
rows.standfirst: The city has challenges and it looks to AI and a whole community to help resolve some of them.

rows.title: What’s Working: Cities like Denver want AI to handle boring, tedious tasks
rows.standfirst: Mayor Mike Johnston shared artificial intelligence examples at this week’s DenAI Summit. Plus: Colorado unemployment rate hits 4%, a $14 million quantum update, reader poll results, more!

rows.title: Amid flurry of newspaper closures on Colorado’s Eastern Plains, Burlington sees a heroic revival
rows.standfirst: But another century-old paper, the Plainsman Herald in Springfield, plans to stop printing at the end of the year

rows.title: Denver’s new “social justice art” is a 5-foot canvas boulder created by people who have lived on the streets
rows.standfirst: The project led by artist Emma Balder is intended to give voice to people who don’t feel seen and will go on display in the spring

rows.title: Thornton’s Solid Power gets $50 million from feds to expand, prove out EV battery technology
rows.standfirst: A growing number of Colorado battery-makers are taking advantage of U.S. and local support to create an industry

rows.title: Broomfield nonprofit agrees to pay $449,999 to 10 workers who were fired after forming a union
rows.standfirst: The food nonprofit Big Green, founded by Kimbal Musk, agreed not to appeal and must require all managers to go through employee-rights training.

rows.title: Colorado had the second highest number of job quitters in July
rows.standfirst: And was tied for fifth for all job separations

rows.title: Colorado oil and gas industry’s most high-profile advocate steps down
rows.standfirst: Colorado Oil and Gas Association head Dan Haley, who often locks horns with Democrats in the legislature, plans to leave his influential post when a successor is found

rows.title: What’s Working: Cooling Colorado Springs’ job economy’s top concern? Affordable housing.
rows.standfirst: Also at this week’s UCCS Economic Forum: Inflation has slowed even if it doesn’t feel like it. Plus: Western Colorado University drops fee

rows.title: A picturesque lake in southwestern Colorado disappeared. Locals want it back as fast as possible.
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Forest Service drained Crystal Lake in April, citing dam issues and concern for public safety. The move left locals flummoxed.
